intro: Wednesday supplied the clearest example this week of why the word “buyer” needs a second question. Carvana's bondholders, short sellers and holders of weekly calls all had reasons to welcome the debt exchange. They own different claims and have different deadlines. The separation matters just as much in two earnings reports released after the bell. Record Tesla vehicle deliveries and new Netflix memberships both need to be translated into cash. [CV] [TSQ] [NFL]

plays.title: Carvana (CVNA) | The shorts have a deadline, too
parts: Why Retail Is Here

A trader buying Wednesday's close at $55.80 is betting on something quite specific. Carvana can sell fewer cars and still be worth more to shareholders if lenders give it time. The shares jumped 40.2% in one session. The attraction is partly the seller on the other side. Someone who borrowed the stock to bet on an imminent financing crisis has to decide how long to hold that position after creditors themselves have backed a deal. Someone buying after the spike needs to think about who will take over when that short seller has finished covering. [CVR] [CV]
What Is Driving It

Holders of over 90% of the unsecured notes signed the transaction support agreement. At the indicated participation level Carvana projects a principal reduction of more than $1.2 billion and over $430 million less required cash interest per year for two years. Some interest would accrue as additional debt. That buys time to fix the dealership. Retail units fell 35% from a year earlier to 76,530; roughly $70 million in nonrecurring items helped the quarterly result. A business can make sensible use of an interest holiday and still emerge with creditors holding the strongest claim on future cash. [CV] [CVE]
The Social Signal

Carvana was fifth in Wednesday morning's 24-hour WallStreetBets mentions. By 10:44 a.m. Eastern, 87,000 calls and 81,000 puts had traded, roughly five times normal options activity for that time. The July $59 call drew the most contracts and included purchases to open. The strike tells us what the late buyer needs. Even after a 40% gain, the close fell short of it. The substantial put turnover also matters. Across those contracts some traders wanted protection or downside exposure. The tape reveals neither the account type of every trader nor a net retail dollar balance. [W19] [CVO] [CVR]
Historical Analog

Think of a refinancing squeeze. When the borrower gains breathing room, the first buyer can be a short seller whose deadline just moved. That buyer only needs to acquire the shares once. The next buyer needs a reason to own a used-car business after the paperwork closes. Where those two buyers hand over is where a spectacular squeeze can run out of money. A second wave of gains is easier to defend if the dealer can retain better unit economics while recovering sales volume. Its adjusted operating result and falling unit count give shareholders a way to check. [CVE] [CVR]
Smart Money View

Apollo's John Zito backed the exchange and singled out the new first-lien debt. That distinction is central to the equity trade. Apollo's side gains a claim on collateral; common shareholders stand behind the lenders and face a planned $350 million equity raise. Both sides can endorse Wednesday's agreement and have very different protection if customers buy fewer cars. The most persuasive feature of the transaction for a bondholder, improved security on the assets, is exactly why the equity owner cannot simply adopt the creditor's enthusiasm as an estimate of common-share value. [CV] [CVR]
When the Narrative Breaks

Watch the $59 calls into expiry. If the shares stall below the strike, a trader can be right about Carvana surviving and still lose the entire premium. The longer-lived test comes at the exchange and the next results. Financing needs to close, and the business needs to deliver the second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA that management expects with less help from one-time items. Cash interest saved can fund operations, but it does not bring a customer onto a lot. Fewer sales with falling unit profitability would reopen the original operating question. [CVO] [CV] [CVE]

plays.title: Tesla (TSLA) | Revenue at a record, the call spread under pressure
parts: The Setup

Wednesday's update put a price on the delivery surge. Companywide gross margin was 18.2%, operating margin 9.6% and quarterly revenue nearly $25 billion. The first two numbers should temper a direct extrapolation from the third. Manufacturing efficiencies and a busier factory can raise the number of vehicles sold, yet discounts and mix still determine how much of that revenue reaches shareholders. Tesla said in its update that reduced average selling prices weighed on operating income. Follow the margin attached to the next increment of volume. [TSQ]
What to Watch

Interactive Brokers reported before the release that Tesla was its most active stock and single-name option class. Friday-expiring at-the-money implied volatility was around 117%. The probability distribution peaked near $290–292 with the stock around $298 when measured. That shows why reporting a good quarter in ordinary business terms is not enough for a short-dated call buyer. The investor paid for a large move and needs it in the right direction. A shareholder can wait several quarters to evaluate the economics of the price cuts. [IB] [TSQ]

plays.title: Netflix (NFLX) | Pricing the extra household
parts: The Setup

Netflix added roughly 5.9 million paid memberships in the second quarter as it broadened the paid-sharing initiative. The company's letter puts revenue at $8.2 billion and operating profit at $1.8 billion. The count of accounts is evidence that people who previously shared passwords can be converted. It does not settle what they pay. Some can join as extra members, others can take a lower-priced advertising plan. The revenue line depends on when they joined, which package they chose and whether advertisers pay enough for the added viewing time. [NFL]
What to Watch

The next useful comparison is revenue growth alongside membership growth through the second half, when management expects more of the benefit to show through. If new accounts remain active and generate incremental revenue, the policy can expand the addressable business without raising list prices for everyone. If the gap persists, there may be more paying accounts but less revenue per account than shareholders expected. Wednesday's premarket Quiver survey ranked Netflix seventh. The audience for the result was visible before any after-hours reaction. [NFL] [W19]

plays.title: Microsoft (MSFT) | Software pricing through the second session
parts: The Setup

Wednesday's premarket Quiver measure ranked Microsoft fourth on WallStreetBets in the wake of its $30-per-user Copilot announcement. The market now has a point of comparison for the rest of enterprise software. A vendor charging per seat has to demonstrate a productivity improvement large enough to justify the add-on. The bigger the customer's organization, the bigger the potential annual contract, but the more likely the buyer is to begin with a limited group and ask to see evidence from the pilot. [W19] [MS]
What to Watch

The first price calculation is easy, and the next one matters more. A thousand fully paid seats at list price would generate $360,000 a year before discounts and costs. That amount cannot be booked simply because a company has a thousand employees with access to Office. Look for the first credible conversion and deployment figures, and for the infrastructure cost of serving those users. If pricing excitement broadens into revenues without a matching expansion of costs, it can support a durable earnings thesis. [MS]
